¡Hola! Soy Ezequiel, un apasionado de la física aplicada, los sistemas complejos y la narrativa interactiva.

Se me ocurre un videojuego interactivo tipo novela visual. El proyecto conectara los artefactos que la NASA ha dejado en el cosmos con los retos de nuestro entorno escolar. Huellas en el espacio
summary:
===Archaeology of the Martian Forest! is an interactive, browser-based visual novel that transforms space exploration history into a relatable school camping trip. Using everyday analogies, players journey from a flat basecamp (Arcadia Planitia) up to a panoramic summit (Olympus Mons), discovering "abandoned, yet not forgotten" artifacts—including the InSight seismometer, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance alongside the Ingenuity drone.
We developed a lightweight, accessible HTML5 and JavaScript visual novel featuring 38 illustrated scenes, player name customization, and interactive audio cues. By translating complex planetary science, laser spectroscopy, and seismic telemetry into casual conversations between classmates, the project directly addresses the challenge of making space exploration engaging and easy to grasp for non-technical audiences.
This project is important because it bridges the gap between raw NASA mission data and everyday curiosity. By celebrating robotic pioneers as enduring milestones of human ingenuity, it inspires students to appreciate past discoveries and envision future interplanetary journeys.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Huellas en el Espacio (Footprints in Space) is a browser-based, click-and-touch interactive visual novel structured across 38 sequential illustrated scenes. Upon starting the expedition, players register their name into the Lunar Camp roster, which dynamically personalizes the dialogue throughout the entire journey. Following a Hohmann transfer route mapped onto a school camping trip, players hike alongside a classmate from the flat landing zone of Arcadia Planitia up to the summit of Olympus Mons, encountering abandoned Martian rovers and landers along the way. By clicking or tapping anywhere on the screen, users unlock conversational explanations that translate real planetary science into everyday analogies—comparing InSight to a medical stethoscope, Opportunity to a solar marathon runner, Curiosity’s ChemCam to fireworks spectroscopy, and Perseverance’s Ingenuity drone to a high-speed hummingbird.

Benefits & Intended Impact
The project removes technical jargon and hardware barriers to space education. Because it runs smoothly on any desktop or mobile browser without requiring installations or heavy downloads, it serves as an immediate educational tool for classrooms, science outreach, and curious learners. Our intended impact is to spark lasting interest in STEM and planetary science by reframing robotic missions not as cold machinery, but as enduring human footprints that pave the way for future explorers.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6).
  • Audio & Interactivity: Web Audio API (for real-time synthesized retro sound effects) and HTML5 Audio.
  • Development & Design Software: Visual Studio Code for programming, digital illustration tools for 3:2 aspect-ratio scene artwork, and NASA’s public mission archives and transcripts for scientific accuracy.

Creativity & Design Considerations
Our core creative approach lies in blending authentic NASA engineering history with relatable Mexican youth slang and camp storytelling. Rather than presenting a dry encyclopedia, we turned complex orbital and geological concepts into a lighthearted peer-to-peer adventure. Key factors considered during development included accessibility (responsive 3:2 layout for both PC and mobile touchscreens), cognitive pacing (short, bite-sized dialogue turns to prevent text fatigue), and scientific rigor (grounding every analogy in real mission telemetry and hardware functions).
